summary: Abdur Rehman is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned his PhD from the Australian National University under Arthur Llewellyn Basham and studied under Ahmad Hasan Dani. In 1988, he held a post at the University of Peshawar.

Abel Bergaigne (1838–1888) was a French Indologist and linguist. He studied under Michel Bréal and Eugène-Louis Hauvette-Besnault. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1869–1877) and the University of Paris as lecturer (1877) and professor (1885).

Abigail I. MacBain works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her MA at McMaster University, studying under Mark Rowe, James A. Benn, Shayne Clarke, Mark MacWilliams, and Michael Greenwald. As of 2026, she holds a post at the University of Edinburgh.

Abraham Hyacinthe Anquetil-Duperron (1731–1805) was a scholar in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Paris, Amersfoort Seminary, and under Dastur Darab, later holding posts at the Bibliothèque nationale, Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres, Académie Française, and Institut de France.

Abraham Sachs (1914–1983) worked in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Johns Hopkins University (~1934–1939) and held appointments at the Institute for Advanced Study (1945) and Brown University (~1948–1983).

Abraham Valentine Williams Jackson (1862–1937) was an Indologist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Columbia University under Edward Washburn Hopkins and at the University of Halle-Wittenberg. He spent his career at Columbia University (1883–1935), serving as professor from 1895.
Abraham Zablocki is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Cornell University and held a post at Agnes Scott College in 2008.

Achim Bayer specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Hamburg (PhD 2005) under Lambert Schmithausen, David P. Jackson, and others. He was a research associate at the University of Munich (2004–2006) and a Research Fellow at Hamburg (attested 2026).

Adalbert Bezzenberger (1851–1922) was a German linguist and Indologist. He earned his doctorate and habilitation at the University of Göttingen under Theodor Benfey, where he was a Privatdozent (1874) before becoming professor (1879) and later rector (1919–1921) at the University of Königsberg.

Adalbert Kuhn (1812–1881) was a German Indologist and linguist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp. He had a long career at Köllnisches Gymnasium from 1837, serving as teacher, professor, and director, and was elected to the Russian and Prussian academies.

Adam Bowles is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who earned his doctorate under Greg Bailey. He served as a senior lecturer in Asian Religions at the University of Queensland (attested 2016–2018).

Adam Hardy (born 1953) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge. He served as Professor of Asian Architecture at Cardiff University (~2000), Director of PRASADA, and editor of South Asian Studies (~2004–2011).

Adam Pearcey is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under Ulrich Pagel, Nathan W. Hill, and Vincent Tournier, and studied under numerous traditional Tibetan teachers, including the 14th Dalai Lama.

Adam Yuet Chau is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who studied at Williams College and Stanford University (PhD 2001). After a postdoctoral fellowship at Harvard, he served as lecturer (attested 2011–2015) and later professor (attested 2026) at the University of Cambridge.

Adelheid Herrmann-Pfandt (born 1955) works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She studied at the Universities of Bonn, Erlangen-Nuremberg, and Marburg, where she habilitated. She held posts as guest professor at the University of Vienna (~2004–2005) and Privatdozentin at Marburg (2009).

Adelheid Mette (1934–2023) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed her doctorate and habilitation at the University of Hamburg. She held professorships at the University of Munich (1978, 1980) and held the Indology chair at the University of Münster (1971, 1988–2000).

Aden Kumler (born 1974) is an art historian and archaeologist who studied at the University of Chicago, University of Toronto, Pontifical Institute of Mediaeval Studies, and Harvard University (PhD ~2007). She taught at the University of Chicago (2007) and became professor at the University of Basel in 2020.
Adeu Rinpoche (1931–2007) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology master. He studied under traditional teachers Khamtrul Rinpoche, Samten Gyatso, and Chögon Rinpoche.

Adhémard Leclère (1853–1917) worked in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He served as Résident de France at Kratie in the French Protectorate of Cambodia and was vice-president of the Société d'ethnologie, which he founded.

Adinath Neminath Upadhye (1906–1975) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Mumbai (BA, D.Litt.) and the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute. He taught at Rajaram College (1930–1962), became Professor Emeritus at Shivaji University (1962–1971), and held the Jaina Chair at the University of Mysore (1971).
